key_insight: scPEFT enables rapid, parameter-efficient adaptation of single-cell large language models by updating only a small fraction of parameters, leading to improved generalization on unseen diseases, treatments and cell types.
problem_solved: Fine-tuning full large models on single-cell data is compute- and data-intensive and often fails to generalize to out-of-distribution biological conditions; scPEFT addresses both efficiency and robustness to unseen conditions.
method: Introduce a parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategy for single-cell LLMs that injects small, trainable modules or low-rank updates while keeping the majority of model weights frozen.
Train on diverse single-cell expression datasets and biological tasks to learn transferable adjustments.
Evaluate transfer performance on held-out diseases, treatments and cell types to demonstrate improved out-of-distribution generalization with minimal parameter updates.
impact: scPEFT lowers the computational and data barrier for adapting large single-cell models, enabling practitioners to deploy and test biologically meaningful models faster and with better OOD performance—facilitating discovery in disease and treatment response.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: frozen base single-cell LLM + small trainable PEFT modules (adapters/low-rank heads) highlighted

Icon set: lower GPU/compute, faster iteration, improved generalization
paper_title: Harnessing the power of single-cell large language models with parameter-efficient fine-tuning using scPEFT
paper_authors: Fei He, Ruixin Fei, Jordan E. Krull, Yang Yu, Xinyu Zhang
